title: Free tutorial: Find a secret in a Git repo
summary: Scan a repository for secrets, including the ones deleted from files but still in Git history.

next.title: Seminar 8: Cloud and DevSecOps: posture, pipelines, secrets and automation

script.intro: Welcome. Keys leak through Git more often than through any clever attack. Here you scan a repository for secrets, including ones that were deleted but are still in the history.
script.outro: Revoke first, clean up after. Seminar 8 builds the pipeline checks that stop this reaching the repository at all.
steps: Read the setting so you know the company, the date and the time zone. Then open the evidence in the case folder.

The scanner looks in three places. Secrets: keys and passwords in files and in Git history. Dependencies: package versions with known advisories. Configuration: the Dockerfile, Kubernetes and Terraform. Scan everything, then read each tab. The important finding is in the history. A patch removed the key from deploy dot sh, but the old line still starts with a minus sign in the diff, and anyone who clones the repo can read it. Deleting a secret never un-leaks it. The fix is to revoke the key and issue a new one.
Revoke first, clean up after. Seminar 8 builds the pipeline checks that stop this reaching the repository at all.
